items.title: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack") Interview, 1959-07-01
items.q: he built the Pike Theater for me... And he used to loan me money too, whenever I was organizing, needed costumes and things.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah. Chicken Jones. Chicken Jones. Chicken Jones. Uh-huh.

There was, uh, some old musicians there. Uh, well, my father used to run a barbershop on Davis Avenue right down. Oh, by the way, in Mobile, there's a man, uh, I don't know, he's probably gone too. His name was Charlie Schreiner, a John Furrier-German fellow. And he built the Pike Theater for me. I just went around the country and I was having people, but they liked me so well, they wanted me to stay around, you see. And so, he said, when you come back here, I'm going to have a theater. I'm building it just…

How did those bands compare with the New Orleans bands when you heard them later? That is, the brass band, did they swing a good deal, you know? I mean, on the street, like the funerals, you talk about coming back, you know, where they'd really swing now. Yeah, yeah. Did the Mobile bands play that same style?
